# Solana Developer Platform

> Full public documentation for Solana Developer Platform — all page content for AI and agent ingestion.

## Canonical URLs
- Docs: https://platform.solana.com/docs
- API: https://api.solana.com
- API reference: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api
- OpenAPI: https://api.solana.com/openapi.json
- AI guide: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/docs-for-ai

## Docs

### What is SDP?
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/introduction

> One API for building on Solana with your chosen providers, from devnet to mainnet.

Solana Developer Platform (SDP) gives your app one API for the Solana services it uses. Build and test on devnet in the dashboard, then call the API with a key you create there.

## Why SDP

Institutional assets are moving onchain. In October 2026, RWA.xyz tracked [about $39.5 billion in tokenized real-world assets](https://app.rwa.xyz/), including [about $5.2 billion on Solana](https://app.rwa.xyz/networks/solana). [Tokenized stocks](https://app.rwa.xyz/stocks) are one part of that growth.

Assets at this scale need custody, enforceable compliance, and auditable controls. SDP puts the services your deployment supports behind one API, so you can build on Solana without wiring up every provider yourself.

## How it fits together

- **Devnet and mainnet** each have their own keys, wallets, and settings. Build on devnet with test tokens, then [go to mainnet](/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet) once SDP approves your organization.
- **Providers** supply the services behind SDP. You choose the providers you use; your app calls the same SDP API either way.
- **Access** is explicit. An API key holds only the actions you grant it, and sensitive operations leave an audit trail.

## What you can build

This deployment publishes these modules:

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Custody** | Provision and operate Solana wallets through interchangeable custody providers |
| **Payments** | Move funds onchain: transfers, batches, recurring payments, and payment requests |

[Get started](/docs) on devnet, or [browse the API reference](/docs/reference/api).

### Go to mainnet
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet

> Request mainnet access, connect your own custody account, and go live.

You start with a Sandbox project on devnet. The SDP team must approve your
organization before enabling Production on mainnet.

## 1. Request mainnet access

Sign in to the [dashboard](https://platform.solana.com/dashboard) as an
**organization admin**. Open the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar, then
**Settings**. Under **Mainnet access**, click **Request mainnet access**. If the
section is missing, ask an admin to submit.

[![The Mainnet access section in organization settings, with Request mainnet access](/images/go-to-mainnet/01-request-access.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/01-request-access.png)

Select your organization's registered **Country or region** and click
**Continue**. Contact the SDP team to change it after submission.

[![Request mainnet access with Singapore selected as the organization's jurisdiction](/images/go-to-mainnet/02-jurisdiction.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/02-jurisdiction.png)

Read the **Terms and Conditions** to the end, accept them on your organization's
behalf, and click **Send request**. **Request sent** confirms submission;
Settings shows **In review** until approval.

[![Request sent confirmation, with SDP review still pending](/images/go-to-mainnet/request-sent.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/request-sent.png)

If you see **Request not sent**, click **Send request again**; your details are
saved. If requests aren't open, contact the SDP team.

## 2. Switch to Production

After approval, refresh **Settings**. When **Mainnet access** shows **Approved**,
click your organization's name at the top of the sidebar and select your
production project (by default, **Default Production Project**).

<a href="/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/03-production-project.png">
  <img
    src="/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/03-production-project.png"
    alt="The workspace switcher showing Default Production Project"
    width="330"
    height="342"
    style={{ maxWidth: "100%", height: "auto" }}
  />
</a>

Production uses `mainnet-beta`. Wallets, provider connections, and API keys are
separate from Sandbox and must be set up again.

## 3. Connect your custody provider account

Production runs on your own provider account. In Production, open **Wallets**,
click **Create wallet**, and select **Privy** if the page asks for a provider.

Keep or rename the **Credential label**. Enter your **Privy app ID** and
**Privy app secret** from the [Privy dashboard](https://dashboard.privy.io),
then a **Wallet label**. Click **Connect and create wallet** to verify the
connection and create your first Privy wallet.

[![Privy credential form with an example app ID and a masked app secret](/images/go-to-mainnet/04-connect-privy.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/04-connect-privy.png)

For more wallets, pick this connection under **Whose Privy account holds the
keys?** See [Create a wallet](/docs/guides/setup-wallets).

## 4. Create a production API key

In Production, open **API keys** and click **Create new API key**. Name it,
grant the actions it needs, choose which wallets it can sign with, and review
the summary. Click **Create key**.

[![API key review showing Production, selected permissions, and the Treasury wallet](/images/go-to-mainnet/05-production-api-key.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/05-production-api-key.png)

Copy the key to your secret manager; it's shown once. Replace your backend's
sandbox key. The API URL stays `https://api.solana.com`; the key's project
determines the network. See
[API key grants and wallet access](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys).

## 5. Fund your wallet with mainnet USDC

Send a small amount of **USDC on Solana mainnet** to your wallet's address.
Devnet tokens have no value on mainnet. Circle's
[mainnet USDC mint](https://developers.circle.com/stablecoins/usdc-contract-addresses)
is `EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v`.

Use `"token": "USDC"` in transfer requests so SDP selects the mint for your network.
Replace any hardcoded devnet mint addresses.

SDP sponsors network fees and recipient token-account rent for transfers it
signs from your Privy wallet. Fund it with USDC; no SOL is needed for those fees.
Sponsorship limits apply. If sponsorship is unavailable, SDP refuses the transfer
instead of charging your wallet.

Send a [small first payment](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment) and
[verify its status](/docs/payments/accept-verification) before increasing volume.

### Core concepts
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/developing-with-sdp

> The interfaces, environments, and conventions you build against.

SDP has two interfaces over the same API:

- **Dashboard:** the browser UI. Sign in with email, Google, or GitHub.
- **REST API:** programmatic access for backend integrations. Requests authenticate with an API key in the `Authorization` header.

Both call the same API, and each route requires the same action whoever calls it. A signed-in member holds actions through their organization role; an API key holds the grants you give it. Some routes are for signed-in members only, such as managing API keys, members, and the organization, or setting up a custody provider. An API key is refused them.

Build against the API for automation and integrations. Use the dashboard to set up your organization, inspect state, and run one-off operations.

## Environments

An environment belongs to the **project**, not to individual requests. Every tenant resource and API key belongs to a project and inherits its environment.

| Environment  | Network      |
| ------------ | ------------ |
| `sandbox`    | devnet       |
| `production` | mainnet-beta |

A key's format doesn't name its environment; the project it belongs to does.

Both environments expose the same route shapes. Build and test against your sandbox project, then move to production with a production project's API key. [Go to mainnet](/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet) covers requesting access and setting up your production wallets and API key.

## Response conventions

Every successful response wraps its payload in a `data` envelope with request metadata:

```json
{
  "data": { ... },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "timestamp": "2026-07-31T12:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

Errors return a machine-readable `code` alongside a human-readable `message`:

```json
{
  "error": { "code": "INVALID_API_KEY", "message": "Invalid API key" },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_..." }
}
```

Include the `requestId` when you report an issue. It links your request to SDP's traces.

## Execution model

For a custody operation, SDP builds the transaction, signs it with the configured custody wallet, and submits it.

## Read next

- [Authentication](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) covers project keys and access checks.
- [API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys) covers grants and wallet scope.

Create a custody wallet, check its balances, and use API key grants to control what an integration can do with it.

### Payments
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments

> Send, accept and reconcile Solana payments from your SDP custody wallets.

Send SOL and SPL tokens from your custody wallets, pay many recipients in one batch, schedule recurring payments, and match what moved to your own records. If you have no custody wallet yet, start with [Set Up Wallets](/docs/guides/setup-wallets).

## What's in this section

- **[How payments work on SDP](/docs/payments/concepts)**: wallets, tokens, fees and the transfer record.
- **Send payments**
  - [Basic payment](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment): one transfer, from the dashboard or the API.
  - [Payment with memo](/docs/payments/send-payment-with-memo): tag a transfer with your order or invoice reference.
  - [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts): pay many recipients and reconcile the run.
- **Accept payments**
  - [Accept overview](/docs/payments/accept-overview): payment links, shared addresses, and finding each payment.
  - [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification): transfer statuses and when a payment is final.
  - [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing): list transfers and match them to your ledger.

Wallet balances and controls are in [Wallet operations](/docs/wallet-operations).

## Underlying API

Payments endpoints live under `/v1/payments`: transfers, transfer batches, recurring payments and wallet balances. Each page here links the endpoints it uses, and the [Payments API reference](/docs/reference/api/payments) lists them all.

## Related

- [End-to-end payment flow](/docs/tutorials/end-to-end-payment-flow): wallet setup through settlement and reconciliation.

## Resources

### Self-hosting
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/self-hosting

> Run the Solana Developer Platform on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose.

Self-hosting runs the full Solana Developer Platform (API, dashboard, docs, database, and cache) on infrastructure you control, from prebuilt container images. You bring your own authentication (Clerk), Solana RPC, and signing provider.

## What you run

The release's `compose.yml` starts six services:

| Service | Image | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `sdp-api` | `sdp-api` | The API, on port `8787` by default. |
| `sdp-web` | `sdp-web` | The dashboard, on port `3000` by default. |
| `sdp-docs` | `sdp-docs` | These docs, on port `3001` by default. |
| `sdp-migrate` | `sdp-api` | Applies pending database migrations, then exits. |
| `postgres` | `postgres:16-alpine` | The bundled database. You can use an external one instead. |
| `redis` | `redis:7-alpine` | The bundled cache. You can use an external one instead. |

## Start here

- [Quickstart](/docs/self-hosting/quickstart): install the stack and bring it up.
- [First devnet deployment](/docs/self-hosting/first-devnet-deployment): sign in to the dashboard, create a local wallet, and call the API with a wallet-scoped key.
- [Configurator](/docs/self-hosting/configurator): generate a complete `.env` in your browser or terminal.
- [Environment reference](/docs/self-hosting/env-reference): what the variables do and which ones are required.

## Operate

- [Upgrade and backup](/docs/self-hosting/upgrade-and-backup): move to a new release and protect your data.
- [Troubleshooting](/docs/self-hosting/troubleshooting): common startup and configuration failures.
- [External co-signers](/docs/self-hosting/external-co-signers): host provider-specific signing services beside the stack.

## Requirements

- A 64-bit Linux or macOS host (x86-64 or Arm64) with Docker Engine and Docker Compose v2.
- Outbound network access to pull images and reach your Solana RPC and Clerk.
- A [Clerk](https://clerk.com) application and a Solana RPC endpoint. The [environment reference](/docs/self-hosting/env-reference) lists the rest.

## Health

### Health
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/health

> Service health and readiness endpoints.

| Method | Endpoint | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/health` | [Health check](/docs/reference/api/health/health-check.md) |

---

### Health check
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/health/health-check

> Returns service health and build metadata.

`GET /health`

Public: this route takes no API key.

## Responses

- **`200`** Service is healthy

  - **`status`** · `string` · required · always `ok`

    Health status.

  - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

    Health check timestamp.

  - **`version`** · `string` · required · example `0.1.0`

    Service version.

  - **`environment`** · `string` · required · example `production`

    Runtime environment.

  - **`releaseChannel`** · `string` · required · one of `experimental`, `beta`, `stable` · example `experimental`

    Release channel: which modules this deployment runs.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/health'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/health", {
  method: "GET"
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import requests

r = requests.get("https://api.solana.com/health")
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"
{
  "status": "ok",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "environment": "production",
  "releaseChannel": "experimental"
}
```

---

### Readiness check
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/health/health-readiness

> Performs readiness checks for downstream dependencies.

`GET /health/ready`

Public: this route takes no API key.

## Responses

- **`200`** Service is ready

  - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `ready`, `not_ready` · example `ready`

    Readiness status.

  - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

    Readiness check timestamp.

  - **`revision`** · `string` · required · example `sdp-prod-api-public-00042-abc`

    Cloud Run revision serving the request, or `local` outside Cloud Run.

  - **`commit`** · `string` · required · example `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`

    Git commit the serving image was built from, or `local` when the image carries none.

  - **`checks`** · `object` · required

    Dependency health checks.

    - **`database`** · `string` · required · one of `ok`, `error` · example `ok`

      Database connectivity status.

    - **`redis`** · `string` · required · one of `ok`, `error` · example `ok`

      Redis connectivity status.

    - **`egress`** · `string` · one of `pending`, `ok`, `unverified` · example `ok`

      Outbound internet connectivity of this instance. `pending` (not ready) while a fresh instance waits for working egress, `ok` once an outbound call succeeded, `unverified` when it stopped waiting and serves anyway. Absent where the deployment does not wait for egress.

- **`503`** Service is not ready

  Same fields as `200`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/health/ready'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/health/ready", {
  method: "GET"
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import requests

r = requests.get("https://api.solana.com/health/ready")
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"
{
  "status": "ready",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "revision": "sdp-prod-api-public-00042-abc",
  "commit": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "checks": {
    "database": "ok",
    "redis": "ok",
    "egress": "ok"
  }
}
```

```json tab="503"
{
  "status": "not_ready",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "revision": "sdp-prod-api-public-00042-abc",
  "commit": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "checks": {
    "database": "ok",
    "redis": "error",
    "egress": "ok"
  }
}
```

### Initialize wallet signing
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/initialize-wallet-signing

> Sets up Managed custody for the project's named provider by creating its active signing configuration and first wallet.

`POST /v1/wallets/initialize`

Production projects use BYOK only: there this returns 403 with details.reason custody_mode_not_allowed, and wallets are created in a Custody Connection with POST /v1/wallets and connectionId.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.configure` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string`

  Use a unique 1–255 printable ASCII key per operation. Reuse it with the same request on retries. An in-flight attempt returns `409`; a changed request returns `422`. [Retry and recovery rules](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency).

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Initialize wallet signing provider for the project resolved from the request context.

One of:

- **provider: "privy"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `privy`

  - **`requestDelayMs`** · `integer` · min 0 · max 3000

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

## Responses

- **`201`** Wallet signing initialized

  - **`configId`** · `string` · required · example `cfg_example`

    Created wallet signing config ID.

  - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

    Public key of the provisioned root wallet.

  - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

    Provider wallet ID of the provisioned root wallet.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.configure` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason. Forbidden: the caller lacks the route's action or the API key is wallet-scoped, or custody setup was refused. A refusal's details.reason names the failed check: custody_mode_not_allowed when a Production project names Managed custody (Production is BYOK only), custody_provider_not_in_release_channel, or provider_not_entitled.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`503`** PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED: the deployment holds no credentials for the provider in the project's environment (details.reason provider_not_configured).

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl -X POST 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/initialize' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "privy"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/initialize", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "provider": "privy"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests, uuid

r = requests.post("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/initialize",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
  json={
    "provider": "privy"
  })
```

## Example responses

```json tab="201"
{
  "configId": "cfg_example",
  "publicKey": "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112",
  "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
}
```

```json tab="403"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS",
    "message": "Missing action: wallets.configure",
    "details": {
      "action": "wallets.configure"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example"
  }
}
```

Error responses use the [standard error shape](/docs/reference/conventions/errors).

---

### Create wallet
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/create-wallet

> Provisions a new wallet under exactly one provider account: the project's Managed config for provider, or the Custody Connection named by connectionId.

`POST /v1/wallets`

A body naming both, or neither, is rejected with `400`.

With an `Idempotency-Key`, SDP never records a second wallet for one key: a retry returns the wallet an earlier attempt recorded, even after the 24-hour key window. A provider that accepts a request id also receives one derived from the key, so it dedupes at the provider.

A provider failure is stored as a `503`, and a new key is a new provider request. A `503` can mean the provider created the wallet before the error. With a provider that accepts no request id, a failure that left no SDP wallet row makes even the same key a new provider request after 24 hours. Before any retry after an ambiguous failure, whatever the key, check `GET /v1/wallets` and, if the wallet is not there, the provider account.

The provider request id and the recorded-wallet lookup both include the credential. After an API key rotation, once the key's 24-hour record has expired, the same key under the new credential is a new provider request and can create a second wallet: list wallets with `GET /v1/wallets` and check the provider account before retrying a create.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.manage` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string`

  Use a unique 1–255 printable ASCII key per operation. Reuse it with the same request on retries. An in-flight attempt returns `409`; a changed request returns `422`. [Retry and recovery rules](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency).

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Create wallet request body. Names exactly one owner: provider (Managed config) or connectionId (Custody Connection); a body naming both, or neither, is rejected with 400.

Any of:

- **Create a wallet under the project's Managed config for provider.** · must not include `connectionId`

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `privy` · example `privy`

    Provider whose Managed config owns the new wallet. A project holds one active config per provider.

  - **`label`** · `string` · max length 100 · example `Mint authority wallet`

    Optional label for the new wallet.

  - **`purpose`** · `string` · one of `transfer`, `fee_payer` · default `transfer`

    What the wallet is for. Defaults to `transfer`, the only purpose a payment, transfer batch or recurring payment can send from.

- **Create a wallet under a Custody Connection.** · must not include `provider`

  - **`connectionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `cconn_123`

    Custody Connection (BYOK) that owns the new wallet.

  - **`label`** · `string` · max length 100 · example `Mint authority wallet`

    Optional label for the new wallet.

  - **`purpose`** · `string` · one of `transfer`, `fee_payer` · default `transfer`

    What the wallet is for. Defaults to `transfer`, the only purpose a payment, transfer batch or recurring payment can send from.

## Responses

- **`201`** Wallet created

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Created wallet response payload.

    - **`wallet`** · `object` · required

      Wallet details.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · example `cwlt_example`

        Wallet record ID.

      - **`custodyConfigId`** · `string` · example `cfg_example`

        Owning custody configuration ID.

      - **`custodyConnectionId`** · `string` · example `cconn_example`

        Owning Custody Connection ID.

      - **`provider`** · `string` · example `privy`

        Wallet signing provider.

      - **`isRuntimeExecutionAllowed`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether SDP currently permits attempting runtime execution through this wallet's owner. This is request-time admission, not Provider health or a success guarantee.

      - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

        Provider wallet ID.

      - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

        Base58-encoded Solana address.

      - **`label`** · `string | null` · required · example `Treasury wallet`

        Optional wallet label.

      - **`purpose`** · `string | null` · required · example `transfer`

        Optional wallet purpose.

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `active`, `inactive` · example `active`

        Wallet status.

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`balances`** · `object[]`

        Tracked token balances when requested and successfully observed. Omitted when the balance lookup is unavailable; an empty array is a successful zero-token result.

        - **`token`** · `string` · required · example `USDC`

          Tracked token symbol.

        - **`mint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

          Tracked token mint address.

        - **`amount`** · `string` · required · example `1250000`

          Raw token amount as a string.

        - **`uiAmount`** · `string` · required · example `1.25`

          Human-readable token balance.

        - **`decimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `6`

          Token decimals.

        - **`usdPrice`** · `number` · example `1`

          Resolved USD price per token when available.

        - **`usdValue`** · `number` · example `125.5`

          Resolved USD value of this balance when pricing is available.

      One of:

      - **Owned by a Managed config.** · must include `custodyConfigId` · must not include `custodyConnectionId`

      - **Owned by a Custody Connection.** · must include `custodyConnectionId` · must not include `custodyConfigId`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.manage` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason. Forbidden: the caller lacks the route's action or the API key is wallet-scoped, or the provider account was refused. A refusal's details.reason names the failed check: custody_mode_not_allowed when provider names a Managed config in a Production project (Production is BYOK only: create the wallet in a Custody Connection with connectionId), custody_provider_not_in_release_channel, or provider_not_entitled.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`503`** Service Unavailable

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl -X POST 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "privy",
    "label": "Treasury wallet",
    "purpose": "transfer"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "provider": "privy",
    "label": "Treasury wallet",
    "purpose": "transfer"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests, uuid

r = requests.post("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
  json={
    "provider": "privy",
    "label": "Treasury wallet",
    "purpose": "transfer"
  })
```

## Example responses

```json tab="201"
{
  "data": {
    "wallet": {
      "id": "cwlt_example",
      "custodyConfigId": "cfg_example",
      "provider": "privy",
      "isRuntimeExecutionAllowed": true,
      "walletId": "privy_wallet_123",
      "publicKey": "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112",
      "label": "Treasury wallet",
      "purpose": "transfer",
      "status": "active",
      "createdAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

```json tab="403"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS",
    "message": "Missing action: wallets.manage",
    "details": {
      "action": "wallets.manage"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example"
  }
}
```

Error responses use the [standard error shape](/docs/reference/conventions/errors).

### Delete wallet
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/delete-wallet

> Deletes the wallet from its exact owning custody target when that Provider supports wallet deletion.

`DELETE /v1/wallets`

Provider, when supplied, is a consistency assertion.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.execute` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string`

  Use a unique 1–255 printable ASCII key per operation. Reuse it with the same request on retries. An in-flight attempt returns `409`; a changed request returns `422`. [Retry and recovery rules](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency).

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Delete wallet request body.

- **`provider`** · `string` · always `privy` · example `privy`

  Optional consistency assertion for the Provider of the wallet being deleted.

- **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

  Provider wallet ID to delete from its exact owning target.

## Responses

- **`200`** Wallet deleted

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Delete wallet response payload.

    - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

      Wallet ID that was deleted.

    - **`deleted`** · `boolean` · required · always `true` · example `true`

      Deletion confirmation flag.

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.execute` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl -X DELETE 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "privy",
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets", {
  method: "DELETE",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "provider": "privy",
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"

r = requests.delete("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
  json={
    "provider": "privy",
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
  })
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"
{
  "data": {
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123",
    "deleted": true
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

```json tab="403"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS",
    "message": "Missing action: wallets.execute",

      "action": "wallets.execute"
```

### List wallets
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/list-wallets

> Lists active wallets under active Config and Connection owners, oldest first.

`GET /v1/wallets`

Provider narrows the list to one custody provider.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.read` action.

## Query parameters

- **`provider`** · `string` · always `privy` · example `privy`

  Wallet signing provider.

- **`includeBalances`** · `boolean`

- **`view`** · `string` · always `summary`

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

## Responses

- **`200`** Wallets

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Wallets list response payload.

    - **`wallets`** · `object[]` · required

      Wallets.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · example `cwlt_example`

        Wallet record ID.

      - **`custodyConfigId`** · `string` · example `cfg_example`

        Owning custody configuration ID.

      - **`custodyConnectionId`** · `string` · example `cconn_example`

        Owning Custody Connection ID.

      - **`provider`** · `string` · example `privy`

        Wallet signing provider.

      - **`isRuntimeExecutionAllowed`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether SDP currently permits attempting runtime execution through this wallet's owner. This is request-time admission, not Provider health or a success guarantee.

      - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

        Provider wallet ID.

      - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

        Base58-encoded Solana address.

      - **`label`** · `string | null` · required · example `Treasury wallet`

        Optional wallet label.

      - **`purpose`** · `string | null` · required · example `transfer`

        Optional wallet purpose.

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `active`, `inactive` · example `active`

        Wallet status.

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`balances`** · `object[]`

        Tracked token balances when requested and successfully observed. Omitted when the balance lookup is unavailable; an empty array is a successful zero-token result.

        - **`token`** · `string` · required · example `USDC`

          Tracked token symbol.

        - **`mint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

          Tracked token mint address.

        - **`amount`** · `string` · required · example `1250000`

          Raw token amount as a string.

        - **`uiAmount`** · `string` · required · example `1.25`

          Human-readable token balance.

        - **`decimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `6`

          Token decimals.

        - **`usdPrice`** · `number` · example `1`

          Resolved USD price per token when available.

        - **`usdValue`** · `number` · example `125.5`

          Resolved USD value of this balance when pricing is available.

      One of:

      - **Owned by a Managed config.** · must include `custodyConfigId` · must not include `custodyConnectionId`

      - **Owned by a Custody Connection.** · must include `custodyConnectionId` · must not include `custodyConfigId`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

### List wallet signing configs

`GET /v1/wallets/configs`

### Aggregate wallet balances
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/aggregate-wallet-balances

> Aggregates tracked balances for active wallets under the same owner-aware inclusion rules as the wallet list, without exposing one aggregate-level owner or runtime-admission value.

`GET /v1/wallets/aggregate`

Returns 503 if any included wallet balance cannot be read, rather than returning an incomplete total.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.read` action.

## Query parameters

- **`provider`** · `string` · always `privy` · example `privy`

  Wallet signing provider.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

## Responses

- **`200`** Aggregated wallet balances

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Aggregated wallet balance response payload.

    - **`aggregate`** · `object` · required

      Aggregated wallet balance summary.

      - **`walletCount`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `3`

        Number of wallets included in the aggregate.

      - **`balances`** · `object[]` · required

        Aggregated tracked token balances across the included wallets.

        - **`token`** · `string` · required · example `USDC`

          Tracked token symbol.

        - **`mint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

          Tracked token mint address.

        - **`amount`** · `string` · required · example `1250000`

          Raw token amount as a string.

        - **`uiAmount`** · `string` · required · example `1.25`

          Human-readable token balance.

        - **`decimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `6`

          Token decimals.

        - **`usdPrice`** · `number` · example `1`

          Resolved USD price per token when available.

        - **`usdValue`** · `number` · example `125.5`

          Resolved USD value of this balance when pricing is available.

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`503`** Service Unavailable

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/aggregate' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY"
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/aggregate", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`
  }
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests

r = requests.get("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/aggregate",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}"})
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"
{
  "data": {
    "aggregate": {
      "walletCount": 3,
      "balances": [
        {
          "token": "USDC",
          "mint": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
          "amount": "1250000",
          "uiAmount": "1.25",
          "decimals": 6,
          "usdPrice": 1,
          "usdValue": 125.5
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

```json tab="403"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS",
    "message": "Missing action: wallets.read",
    "details": {
      "action": "wallets.read"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example"
  }
}
```

Error responses use the [standard error shape](/docs/reference/conventions/errors).

### Get wallet public key
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/get-wallet-public-key

> Returns the persisted public key for an exact active walletId. walletId is required (400 without it); an API key with selected wallets gets 404 for a wallet it does not list.

`GET /v1/wallets/public-key`

Resolution is DB-backed only.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.read` action.

## Query parameters

- **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

  Provider wallet ID — the `walletId` field returned by GET /v1/wallets.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

## Responses

- **`200`** Wallet public key

  - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

    Base58-encoded Solana address.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/public-key?walletId=privy_wallet_123' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY"
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/public-key?walletId=privy_wallet_123", {
  method: "GET",

    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`
  }
});
```

```json tab="200"
    }
```

### Check signer via simulated memo transaction
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/check-wallet-signer

> Signs a server-authored memo message with the named wallet, verifies the signature, and simulates the transaction.

`POST /v1/wallets/signer-check`

Nothing is broadcast and no sponsorship is spent. The wallet is the only readonly signer and the request cannot supply memo text.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.execute` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string`

  Use a unique 1–255 printable ASCII key per operation. Reuse it with the same request on retries. An in-flight attempt returns `409`; a changed request returns `422`. [Retry and recovery rules](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency).

## Request body

`application/json` · required

walletId is the Provider wallet ID to check, required. Ambiguous Provider IDs are rejected; the check uses the resolved exact custody wallet record, and an API key may check only a wallet within its wallet scope.

- **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1

## Responses

- **`200`** Signer check verified in simulation

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Signer check response payload.

    - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

      Resolved signing wallet ID.

    - **`walletAddress`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

      Resolved signer address used for the check message.

    - **`feePayer`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

      Funded fee payer address used in the simulated message; nothing is spent from it.

    - **`memo`** · `string` · required · example `SDP signer check 123e4567-e89b-42d3-a456-426614174000`

      Server-generated memo text in the simulated check message.

    - **`signature`** · `string` · required · example `sig_example`

      The custody wallet's Ed25519 signature over the check message, base58. Verified server-side and exercised in RPC simulation only — the check never broadcasts, so this signature does not exist on chain.

    - **`simulated`** · `boolean` · required · always `true`

      Always true: signer checks run in simulation and cannot spend sponsorship.

    - **`checkedAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2026-02-20T00:00:00.000Z`

      Timestamp recorded after the simulation succeeded.

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.execute` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`429`** Too Many Requests

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`502`** Bad Gateway

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl -X POST 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/signer-check' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/signer-check", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests, uuid

r = requests.post("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/signer-check",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
  json={
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
  })
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"
{
  "data": {
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123",
    "walletAddress": "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112",
    "feePayer": "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112",
    "memo": "SDP signer check 123e4567-e89b-42d3-a456-426614174000",
    "signature": "sig_example",
    "simulated": true,
    "checkedAt": "2026-02-20T00:00:00.000Z"
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

```json tab="403"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS",
    "message": "Missing action: wallets.execute",
    "details": {
      "action": "wallets.execute"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example"
  }
}
```

Error responses use the [standard error shape](/docs/reference/conventions/errors).

### Get wallet by ID
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/get-wallet-by-id

> Returns active wallet metadata, exact Config or Connection ownership, runtime execution admission, Provider, public key, and by default the current SOL balance.

`GET /v1/wallets/{walletId}`

If the balance read fails, returns 503 instead of a zero balance. Set includeBalance=false for a metadata-only read.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.read` action.

## Path parameters

- **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

  Provider wallet ID — the `walletId` field returned by GET /v1/wallets.

## Query parameters

- **`includeBalance`** · `string` · one of `true`, `false` · example `false`

  Whether to resolve the current SOL balance. Defaults to true; false returns metadata without balance RPC or pricing calls.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

## Responses

- **`200`** Wallet details

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Wallet details by ID response payload.

    - **`wallet`** · `object` · required

      Wallet details with provider and optional SOL balance.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · example `cwlt_example`

        Wallet record ID.

      - **`custodyConfigId`** · `string` · example `cfg_example`

        Owning custody configuration ID.

      - **`custodyConnectionId`** · `string` · example `cconn_example`

        Owning Custody Connection ID.

      - **`provider`** · `string` · required · example `privy`

        Wallet custody provider.

      - **`isRuntimeExecutionAllowed`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether SDP currently permits attempting runtime execution through this wallet's owner. This is request-time admission, not Provider health or a success guarantee.

      - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

        Provider wallet ID.

      - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

        Base58-encoded Solana address.

      - **`label`** · `string | null` · required · example `Treasury wallet`

        Optional wallet label.

      - **`purpose`** · `string | null` · required · example `transfer`

        Optional wallet purpose.

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `active`, `inactive` · example `active`

        Wallet status.

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`balance`** · `object`

        Current SOL balance for the wallet public key. Omitted when includeBalance=false.

        - **`token`** · `string` · required · always `SOL` · example `SOL`

          Balance token symbol.

        - **`mint`** · `string` · required · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

          Native SOL mint address.

        - **`amount`** · `string` · required · example `123456789`

          Raw lamports balance as a string.

        - **`uiAmount`** · `string` · required · example `0.123456789`

          Human-readable SOL balance.

        - **`decimals`** · `number` · required · always `9` · example `9`

          Token decimals for SOL.

      One of:

      - **Owned by a Managed config.** · must include `custodyConfigId` · must not include `custodyConnectionId`

      - **Owned by a Custody Connection.** · must include `custodyConnectionId` · must not include `custodyConfigId`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`503`** Service Unavailable

  Same fields as `401`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/privy_wallet_123' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY"
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/privy_wallet_123", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`
  }
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests

r = requests.get("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/privy_wallet_123",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}"})
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"
{
  "data": {
    "wallet": {
      "id": "cwlt_example",
      "custodyConfigId": "cfg_example",
      "provider": "privy",
      "isRuntimeExecutionAllowed": true,
      "walletId": "privy_wallet_123",
      "publicKey": "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112",
      "label": "Treasury wallet",
      "purpose": "transfer",
      "status": "active",
      "createdAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

```json tab="403"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS",
    "message": "Missing action: wallets.read",
    "details": {
      "action": "wallets.read"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example"
  }
}
```

Error responses use the [standard error shape](/docs/reference/conventions/errors).

### Update wallet
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/update-wallet

> Updates the display label of an active wallet under its exact Config or Connection owner.

`PATCH /v1/wallets/{walletId}`

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.manage` action.

## Path parameters

- **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

  Provider wallet ID — the `walletId` field returned by GET /v1/wallets.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string`

  Use a unique 1–255 printable ASCII key per operation. Reuse it with the same request on retries. An in-flight attempt returns `409`; a changed request returns `422`. [Retry and recovery rules](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency).

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Update wallet request body.

- **`label`** · `string | null` · max length 100 · example `Treasury signer`

  Optional wallet label. Set to null to clear the label.

## Responses

- **`200`** Wallet updated

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Created wallet response payload.

    - **`wallet`** · `object` · required

      Wallet details.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · example `cwlt_example`

        Wallet record ID.

      - **`custodyConfigId`** · `string` · example `cfg_example`

        Owning custody configuration ID.

      - **`custodyConnectionId`** · `string` · example `cconn_example`

        Owning Custody Connection ID.

      - **`provider`** · `string` · example `privy`

        Wallet signing provider.

      - **`isRuntimeExecutionAllowed`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether SDP currently permits attempting runtime execution through this wallet's owner. This is request-time admission, not Provider health or a success guarantee.

      - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

        Provider wallet ID.

      - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

        Base58-encoded Solana address.

      - **`label`** · `string | null` · required · example `Treasury wallet`

        Optional wallet label.

      - **`purpose`** · `string | null` · required · example `transfer`

        Optional wallet purpose.

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `active`, `inactive` · example `active`

        Wallet status.

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`balances`** · `object[]`

        Tracked token balances when requested and successfully observed. Omitted when the balance lookup is unavailable; an empty array is a successful zero-token result.

        - **`token`** · `string` · required · example `USDC`

          Tracked token symbol.

        - **`mint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

          Tracked token mint address.

        - **`amount`** · `string` · required · example `1250000`

          Raw token amount as a string.

        - **`uiAmount`** · `string` · required · example `1.25`

          Human-readable token balance.

        - **`decimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `6`

          Token decimals.

        - **`usdPrice`** · `number` · example `1`

          Resolved USD price per token when available.

        - **`usdValue`** · `number` · example `125.5`

          Resolved USD value of this balance when pricing is available.

      One of:

      - **Owned by a Managed config.** · must include `custodyConfigId` · must not include `custodyConnectionId`

      - **Owned by a Custody Connection.** · must include `custodyConnectionId` · must not include `custodyConfigId`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.manage` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl -X PATCH 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/privy_wallet_123' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "label": "Treasury signer"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/privy_wallet_123", {
  method: "PATCH",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "label": "Treasury signer"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests, uuid

r = requests.patch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/privy_wallet_123",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
  json={
    "label": "Treasury signer"
  })
```

```json tab="200"
      "walletId": "privy_wallet_123",
      "publicKey": "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112",
      "label": "Treasury wallet",
      "purpose": "transfer",
      "status": "active",
      "createdAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
    }
```

Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/projects/list-projects

> Lists projects in the organization.

`GET /v1/projects`

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `projects.read` action.

## Query parameters

- **`includeArchived`** · `boolean` · example `false`

  Include archived resources in results.

## Responses

- **`200`** Projects list

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    List of projects.

    - **`projects`** · `object[]` · required

      Projects.

        Project identifier.

      - **`organizationId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `org_example`

        Organization identifier.

      - **`name`** · `string` · required · example `Payments`

        Project name.

      - **`slug`** · `string` · required · example `payments`

        URL-friendly slug.

      - **`description`** · `string | null` · required · example `Payments workflow`

        Optional project description.

      - **`environment`** · `string` · required · one of `sandbox`, `beta`, `production` · example `sandbox`

        Project environment.

      - **`settings`** · `object | null` · required

        Project settings, or null when none have been set.

          Webhook URL for event notifications.

        - **`metadata`** · `object`

          Arbitrary metadata key/value pairs.

          - **`*`** · `string`

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `active`, `archived` · example `active`

        Project status.

      - **`createdBy`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `usr_example`

        Identifier of the creator.

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        Creation timestamp.

      - **`updatedAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-02T00:00:00.000Z`

      Machine-readable error code.

Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

### Update project
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/projects/update-project

> Updates project attributes.

`PATCH /v1/projects/{projectId}`

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `projects.manage` action.

  Project identifier.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Update project request body.

- **`name`** · `string` · min length 1 · max length 100 · example `Payments Updated`

  Updated project name.

- **`description`** · `string | null` · max length 500 · example `Updated project description.`

  Updated description. Use null to clear.

- **`settings`** · `object | null`

  Updated project settings. Use null to clear.

  - **`webhookUrl`** · `string` · format `uri`

  - **`metadata`** · `object`

    - **`*`** · `string`

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

      Project details.

        Project identifier.

      - **`organizationId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `org_example`

        Organization identifier.

      - **`name`** · `string` · required · example `Payments`

        Project name.

      - **`slug`** · `string` · required · example `payments`

        URL-friendly slug.

      - **`description`** · `string | null` · required · example `Payments workflow`

        Optional project description.

      - **`environment`** · `string` · required · one of `sandbox`, `beta`, `production` · example `sandbox`

        Project environment.

      - **`settings`** · `object | null` · required

        Project settings, or null when none have been set.

        - **`webhookUrl`** · `string` · format `uri` · example `https://example.com/webhook`

          Webhook URL for event notifications.

        - **`metadata`** · `object`

          Arbitrary metadata key/value pairs.

          - **`*`** · `string`

        Project status.

      - **`createdBy`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `usr_example`

        Last update timestamp.

    Response metadata.

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

    Standard error payload.

      Machine-readable error code.

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `projects.manage` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

### Get project provider availability
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/projects/get-project-provider-availability

> Lists every provider this deployment's release channel publishes, with whether this project can use it, counting the deployment's provider credentials for the project's environment.

`GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/provider-availability`

The same rule gates every provider entry point, so a provider reported unavailable is refused there with 403, or 503 when the deployment does not hold its credentials. A project outside the caller's organization, or another project for a project-bound API key, returns 404.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `projects.read` action.

## Path parameters

- **`projectId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Project identifier.

## Responses

- **`200`** Project provider availability

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Every provider this deployment's release channel publishes, with whether this project can use it; a provider the channel leaves out is omitted, matching this document. Custody entries list the custody modes the project can set the provider up in (empty when none) in `modes`, and each refused mode with the first failed check in `unavailableModes`; every other entry carries `available`, plus `reason` naming the first failed check when unavailable. A provider is available only when the deployment's release channel includes it, SDP currently offers it, the organization is entitled to it, and the deployment holds its credentials for the project's environment; the release channel offers the same providers to Sandbox and Production projects. Custody `modes` include `managed` only in a Sandbox project whose deployment holds the provider's credentials; `byok` runs on the organization's own credentials and is the only mode a Production project can use.

    - **`projectId`** · `string` · required

    - **`environment`** · `string` · required · one of `sandbox`, `production`

    - **`providers`** · `object[]` · required

      One of:

      - **family: "custody"**

        - **`family`** · `string` · required · always `custody`

        - **`provider`** · `string` · required

        - **`modes`** · `string[]` · required · each one of `managed`, `byok`

        - **`unavailableModes`** · `object[]` · required

          - **`mode`** · `string` · required · one of `managed`, `byok`

          - **`reason`** · `string` · required · one of `custody_provider_not_in_release_channel`, `custody_mode_not_allowed`, `provider_not_entitled`, `provider_not_in_release_channel`, `provider_not_offered`, `provider_not_configured`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `projects.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `401`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/v1/projects/prj_example/provider-availability' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY"
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/projects/prj_example/provider-availability", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`
  }
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests

r = requests.get("https://api.solana.com/v1/projects/prj_example/provider-availability",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}"})
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"
{
  "data": {
    "projectId": "prj_example",
    "environment": "production",
    "providers": [
      {
        "family": "custody",
        "provider": "privy",
        "modes": [
          "byok"
        ],
        "unavailableModes": [
          {
            "mode": "managed",
            "reason": "custody_mode_not_allowed"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

```json tab="403"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS",
    "message": "Missing action: projects.read",
    "details": {
      "action": "projects.read"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_example"
  }
}
```

Error responses use the [standard error shape](/docs/reference/conventions/errors).
